# Question: generator-shortcuts

> For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival rule that
> fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it disagrees
> with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your proposed
> generator emits such cases.

## Answer

The strongest plausible shortcut I found is
`repeated_cell_count_else_first_panel`:

1. Find the largest object in each panel.
2. If exactly two of those objects have the same cell count, output the
   D4-canonical form of one of that pair.
3. Otherwise, output the D4-canonical form of panel 0.

This is stronger than “always use panel 0.” It matches every canonical
input/output pair because panel 0 is common in all three canonical examples, and
it matched every ordinary v1.4 generated example because v1.4 always gave the
common pair one cell count and the distractor a different count.

An exact disagreement input emitted by the repaired generator is:

```text
[
  [2,0,0,0, 5, 0,0,0,0, 5, 0,0,4,4],
  [2,2,0,0, 5, 0,0,0,3, 5, 0,0,4,0],
  [0,2,0,0, 5, 0,3,3,3, 5, 0,0,4,0],
  [0,0,0,0, 5, 0,0,0,0, 5, 0,0,0,0],
  [0,0,0,0, 5, 0,0,0,0, 5, 0,0,0,0]
]
```

It is generated at seed `314159`, sample index `0`, difficulty `medium`, with
exact overrides:

```text
grid_h=5, panel_w=4, common_cells=4, common_pair="1,2",
palette_kind="default", secondary_objects="none"
```

All three largest objects have four cells, so the shortcut cannot identify a
repeated cell count and falls back to panel 0. Panels 1 and 2 actually share the
D4 class. The intended output is:

```text
[
  [8,8,8],
  [8,0,0]
]
```

The rival returns:

```text
[
  [8,8,0],
  [0,8,8]
]
```

I checked the intended answer three ways: the independent task-local oracle, the
Python `rule_mirror`, and the selected Racket authority through `rule_smoke` and
the source-bound semantic/counterexample checks. The exact fixture, generator
SHA-256, input, outputs, seed, and overrides are retained in
`repo/generators/1cbcf1ed9a32/counterexamples/repeated_cell_count_else_first_panel.json`,
and a focused regression test loads that file and verifies the disagreement.

Yes, the repaired generator emits these cases routinely. Two of every four
scheduled profiles use `common_pair="1,2"`, all generated largest objects have
the same cell count, and the full semantic smoke observed the shared
`panel_zero_distractor` witness 305 times in 600 inputs. The exact-period census
and 100-per-band census found no surviving declared rival in any production or
query-rotation lesson.
